problems.problem: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be real numbers. Prove that the following two statements are equivalent: (i) $a_i+a_j\ge0$ for every pair of distinct indices $i,j$; (ii) for all non-negative real numbers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ with $x_1+\cdots+x_n=1$, $$a_1x_1+\cdots+a_nx_n\ge a_1x_1^2+\cdots+a_nx_n^2.$$

In triangle $ABC$, the altitude $AD$ has length $12$ and the internal bisector $AE$ of $\angle A$ has length $13$. Let $m$ be the length of the median $AF$. Determine the range of $m$ when $\angle A$ is acute, right, and obtuse, respectively.
Let $z_1,\ldots,z_n$ be complex numbers such that $|z_1|+\cdots+|z_n|=1$. Prove that there is a subset of these complex numbers whose sum has modulus at least $\frac16$.

A triangle $ABC$ has area $1$. The four vertices of a quadrilateral $P_1P_2P_3P_4$ lie on the sides of $ABC$. Prove that at least one of the triangles $P_1P_2P_3$, $P_1P_2P_4$, $P_1P_3P_4$, and $P_2P_3P_4$ has area at most $\frac14$.

Determine, with proof, whether the sequence $1,1,2,2,3,3,\ldots,1986,1986$ can be rearranged so that, for every integer $k$ with $1\le k\le1986$, there are exactly $k$ numbers between the two occurrences of $k$.
Every point in the plane is coloured either white or black. Prove that there is an equilateral triangle of side length $1$ or $\sqrt3$ whose three vertices have the same colour.
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Prove that $z^{n+1}-z^n-1=0$ has a root with $|z|=1$ if and only if $6$ divides $n+2$.

An equilateral triangle $ABC$ of side length $n$ is divided into $n^2$ unit equilateral triangles by lines parallel to its sides. Every vertex of these unit triangles is labelled with a real number; $A,B,C$ have labels $a,b,c$, respectively. In every rhombus formed by two unit triangles sharing a side, the sums of the labels on the two pairs of opposite vertices are equal. (a) Determine the shortest distance between a vertex with the largest label and a vertex with the smallest label. (b) Determine the sum of all labels.

In a tournament, every pair of players plays exactly once, and there are no ties. A player $A$ receives a prize if, for every other player $B$, either $A$ defeats $B$, or $A$ defeats a player $C$ who defeats $B$. Prove that if exactly one player receives a prize, that player defeats every other player.

Five points lie inside an equilateral triangle of area $1$. Prove that three equilateral triangles homothetic to the given triangle can cover all five points, with each point inside at least one of them and with the sum of their areas at most $0.64$.

A sphere centred at $O$ is tangent to all six edges of a tetrahedron. Four spheres centred at its four vertices are pairwise externally tangent, and all four are tangent to another sphere centred at $O$. Prove that the tetrahedron is regular.
The sum of $m$ distinct positive even integers and $n$ distinct positive odd integers is $1987$. Find the maximum possible value of $3m+4n$.

Let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be real numbers, not all zero. Determine all real numbers $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ such that, for every choice of real numbers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, $$\sum_{i=1}^n r_i(x_i-a_i)\le\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2}-\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2}.$$

Two concentric circles have radii $r$ and $2r$. A convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in the smaller circle. The extensions of $AB,BC,CD,DA$ meet the larger circle at $C_1,D_1,A_1,B_1$, respectively. (a) Prove that the perimeter of $A_1B_1C_1D_1$ is at least twice that of $ABCD$. (b) Determine when equality holds.

In a sequence of $n$ real numbers, a dragon is a nonempty block of consecutive terms whose average exceeds $1988$; its head is its first term. A single term exceeding $1988$ is also a dragon. Suppose at least one dragon exists. Prove that the average of all terms that are heads of at least one dragon exceeds $1988$.

(a) Let $a_1,a_2,a_3>0$ satisfy $$(a_1^2+a_2^2+a_3^2)^2>2(a_1^4+a_2^4+a_3^4).$$ Prove that they are the side lengths of a triangle. (b) Let $n>3$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n>0$ satisfy $$\left(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2\right)^2>(n-1)\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^4.$$ Prove that any three with distinct indices are the side lengths of a triangle.

For $i=1,2,3$, let $A_iB_iC_iD_i$ be a tetrahedron. Through $B_i,C_i,D_i$, respectively, draw planes perpendicular to $A_iB_i,A_iC_i,A_iD_i$. Suppose all nine planes pass through a common point, and $A_1,A_2,A_3$ are collinear. Determine the intersection of the circumspheres of the three tetrahedra.

For an integer $n\ge3$, let $f(n)$ be the least positive integer that does not divide $n$. Put $f^{(1)}(n)=f(n)$, and whenever $f^{(j)}(n)\ge3$, define $f^{(j+1)}(n)=f(f^{(j)}(n))$. For each $n\ge3$, determine the index $k$ for which $f^{(k)}(n)=2$.

Each of $A,B$ is a union of pairwise disjoint arcs of the unit circle. Every arc in $B$ has length $\pi/m$, where $m$ is a fixed positive integer. Let $A^j$ be the rotation of $A$ counterclockwise through $j\pi/m$. Prove that there is a positive integer $k$ such that $$\ell(A^k\cap B)\ge\frac1{2\pi}\ell(A)\ell(B),$$ where $\ell$ denotes total arc length.
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ be positive real numbers with $x_1+\cdots+x_n=1$. Prove that $$\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{x_i}{\sqrt{1-x_i}}\ge\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n\sqrt{x_i}}{\sqrt{n-1}}.$$

On the unit circle $S$ in the complex plane, define $f(z)=z^m$, where $m$ is a positive integer. Put $f^{(0)}(z)=z$ and $f^{(k+1)}(z)=f(f^{(k)}(z))$. The period of $z$ is the smallest positive integer $n$ with $f^{(n)}(z)=z$, if such an integer exists. Determine the number of points of $S$ with period $1989$.

Triangle $ABC$ has inradius $r$. Points $D,E,F$ lie on $BC,CA,AB$, respectively. If triangles $AEF,BFD,CDE$ have equal inradii, prove that their common inradius is $r-r\prime$, where $r\prime$ is the inradius of triangle $DEF$.

Given $1989$ points in the plane, no three collinear, how should they be partitioned into $30$ groups of distinct sizes to maximise the number of triangles whose three vertices belong to different groups?
Let $S=(1,\infty)$. Determine all functions $f:S\to S$ such that $$f(x^my^n)\le f(x)^{1/(4m)}f(y)^{1/(4n)}$$ for all real $x,y>1$ and $m,n>0$.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with $AB$ not parallel to $CD$. A circle through $A,B$ is tangent to $CD$ at $P$, and a circle through $C,D$ is tangent to $AB$ at $Q$. Prove that the common chord of the circles bisects $PQ$ if and only if $AD\parallel BC$.

A $D$-chain of a positive integer $x$, of length $d$, is a sequence $$1=x_0<x_1<\cdots<x_d=x$$ such that $x_i\mid x_{i+1}$ for $1\le i\le d-1$. For $x=5^k31^m1990^n$, where $k,m,n$ are positive integers, find (a) the maximum length of a $D$-chain; (b) the number of chains of that length.
Let $f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $$f(x)f(y)\le y^2f(x/2)+x^2f(y/2)$$ for all $x\ge y>0$, and suppose $|f(x)|\le M$ for $0\le x\le1$, where $M$ is a fixed constant. Prove that $f(x)\le x^2$.

Let $a$ be a positive integer and $A,B$ real numbers. Find a necessary and sufficient condition on $A,B$ for the system $$x^2(Ax^2+By^2)+y^2(Ay^2+Bz^2)+z^2(Az^2+Bx^2)=\frac14(2A+B)(13a)^4,$$ $$x^2+y^2+z^2=(13a)^2$$ to have a solution in positive integers $x,y,z$.

For a finite set $X$, let $E(X)$ be its subsets of even cardinality. A function $f:E(X)\to\mathbb R$ satisfies $f(D)>1990$ for at least one $D\in E(X)$ and $$f(A\cup B)=f(A)+f(B)-1990$$ whenever $A,B\in E(X)$ are disjoint. Prove that $X$ can be partitioned into disjoint sets $P,Q$ such that $f(S)>1990$ for every nonempty $S\in E(P)$ and $f(T)\le1990$ for every $T\in E(Q)$.

A convex $n$-gon is triangulated by $n-3$ diagonals, no two crossing except at vertices. Prove that there is such a triangulation whose sides and diagonals can all be traversed exactly once in a continuous closed polygonal walk if and only if $3$ divides $n$.

(a) Determine the conditions on a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ under which there is a point $P$ in its plane such that triangles $ABP,BCP,CDP,DAP$ have equal areas. (b) For a given quadrilateral, what is the largest possible number of such points $P$?

Find all functions $f:[0,1]\times[0,1]\to[0,1]$ such that, for all $x,y,z\in[0,1]$, $$f(x,1)=x,\qquad f(1,y)=y,$$ $$f(f(x,y),z)=f(x,f(y,z)),$$ and $$f(zx,zy)=z^kf(x,y),$$ where $k$ is a positive constant independent of $x,y,z$.
Ten birds are at points on a plane. Among any five birds, at least four lie on some circle. What is the minimum possible value of the largest number of these ten birds lying on a circle?
Find all quadruples $(n,x,y,z)$ of positive integers with $n\ge2$, $z\le5\cdot2^{2n}$ and $$x^{2n+1}-y^{2n+1}=xyz+2^{2n+1}.$$
Find all positive integers $n$ such that $$\min_{k\in\mathbb Z_{>0}}\left(k^2+\left\lfloor\frac n{k^2}\right\rfloor\right)=1991.$$

Each vertex of a polyhedron is incident with exactly three edges. Its edges can be coloured with three colours so that at every vertex the three incident edges have different colours. Prove that complex numbers different from $1$ can be assigned to its vertices so that, on every face, the product of the numbers assigned to its vertices is $1$.
Let $0<a_0\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_{n-1}\le1$ be real numbers. If $\lambda$ is a complex root of $$x^n+a_{n-1}x^{n-1}+\cdots+a_1x+a_0=0$$ with $|\lambda|\ge1$, prove that $\lambda^{n+1}=1$.

Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ be nonnegative real numbers, and put $a=\min_i x_i$. With cyclic subscripts, prove that $$\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{1+x_i}{1+x_{i+1}}\le n+\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n(x_i-a)^2}{(1+a)^2},$$ and prove that equality holds if and only if $x_1=\cdots=x_n$.

Each cell of a $9\times9$ board initially contains $1$ or $-1$. In one operation, every cell is simultaneously replaced by the product of the numbers in the cells sharing an edge with it. Is it always possible, after finitely many operations, to make all $81$ numbers equal to $1$?

A convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in a circle with centre $O$. Its diagonals meet at $P$. The circumcircles of triangles $ABP,CDP$ meet again at $Q$. If $O,P,Q$ are distinct, prove that $OQ\perp PQ$.
A graph on $8$ vertices has no loops, multiple edges, or cycles of length $4$. What is the maximum possible number of edges?

Let $a_0,a_1$ be integers, put $a_2=2a_1-a_0+2$, and define $$a_{n+1}=3a_n-3a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}\qquad(n\ge2).$$ Suppose that, for every positive integer $m$, the sequence contains $m$ consecutive terms that are all perfect squares. Prove that every term is a perfect square.

Let $n$ be an odd positive integer. Prove that there are integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n,b_1,\ldots,b_n$ such that, for every integer $k$ with $0\le k<n$, the following $3n$ integers are pairwise incongruent modulo $3n$: $$a_i+a_{i+1},\qquad a_i+b_i,\qquad b_i+b_{i+k}\qquad(1\le i\le n),$$ with subscripts interpreted modulo $n$.

Let $n$ be a positive integer and $a>0$ a real number. Determine the maximum possible value of $$a^{k_1}+a^{k_2}+\cdots+a^{k_s},$$ where $1\le s\le n$, the $k_i$ are positive integers, and $k_1+\cdots+k_s=n$.

Two concentric circles have radii $R<R_1$. Quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in the smaller circle and $A_1B_1C_1D_1$ in the larger, with $A_1,B_1,C_1,D_1$ on the extensions of $CD,DA,AB,BC$, respectively. Prove that $$\frac{[A_1B_1C_1D_1]}{[ABCD]}\ge\frac{R_1^2}{R^2},$$ where $[P]$ denotes the area of polygon $P$.

Let $S$ be a set of $1993$ nonzero vectors in the plane. Prove that $S$ can be partitioned into nonempty subsets such that the angle between every vector in a subset and the sum of the vectors of that subset is at most $90^\circ$, while the angle between the vector sums of any two subsets is greater than $90^\circ$.
Ten people each buy three different books. Every pair of people buys at least one book in common. What is the minimum possible number of buyers of the most frequently purchased book?

Let $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ satisfy $f(xy)\le f(x)f(y)$ for all positive real $x,y$. Prove that, for every positive real $x$ and every positive integer $n$, $$f(x^n)\le\prod_{j=1}^n f(x^j)^{1/j}.$$

Let $ABCD$ be a trapezoid with $AB\parallel CD$. Points $E$ and $F$ lie on segments $AB$ and $CD$, respectively. Let $H=CE\cap BF$ and $G=ED\cap AF$, where the intersections are of the indicated segments. Writing $S$ for area, prove that $$S_{EHFG}\le\frac14 S_{ABCD}.$$ Does the same conclusion hold if $ABCD$ is an arbitrary convex quadrilateral? Justify your answer.

At least four candies are distributed among $n$ plates, where $n\ge4$. A move consists of taking one candy from each of two distinct plates and placing both candies in a third plate. Can all the candies be collected in one plate after finitely many moves? Prove your conclusion.
Find all functions $f:[1,\infty)\to[1,\infty)$ satisfying $$f(x)\le2(x+1),\qquad f(x+1)=\frac{f(x)^2-1}{x}$$ for every real $x\ge1$.

Let $$f(z)=c_0z^n+c_1z^{n-1}+\cdots+c_{n-1}z+c_n$$ be a polynomial of positive degree $n$ with complex coefficients. Prove that there is a complex number $z_0$ with $|z_0|\le1$ such that $$|f(z_0)|\ge|c_0|+|c_n|.$$

For every positive integer $n$, prove that $$\sum_{k=0}^{n}\binom{n}{k}2^k\binom{n-k}{\left\lfloor(n-k)/2\right\rfloor}=\binom{2n+1}{n}.$$ Here $\binom00=1$ and $\lfloor t\rfloor$ denotes the greatest integer not exceeding $t$.

Let $p$ be a prime and let $M=(1994p,7\cdot1994p)$ in the coordinate plane. Find the number of right triangles whose three vertices have integer coordinates, whose right-angle vertex is $M$, and whose incenter is the origin.

Let $a_1,\ldots,a_n,b_1,\ldots,b_n$ be real numbers, where $n\ge3$, satisfying $$\sum_{i=1}^n a_i=\sum_{i=1}^n b_i,$$ $$0<a_1=a_2,\qquad a_i+a_{i+1}=a_{i+2}\quad(1\le i\le n-2),$$ and $$0<b_1\le b_2,\qquad b_i+b_{i+1}\le b_{i+2}\quad(1\le i\le n-2).$$ Prove that $a_{n-1}+a_n\le b_{n-1}+b_n$.

Let $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ satisfy $f(1)=1$ and, for every $n\in\mathbb N$, $$3f(n)f(2n+1)=f(2n)(1+3f(n)),\qquad f(2n)<6f(n).$$ Find all solutions of $f(k)+f(l)=293$ with $k<l$. Here $\mathbb N$ denotes the natural numbers.
Find the minimum value of $$\sum_{i=1}^{10}\sum_{j=1}^{10}\sum_{k=1}^{10}\left|k(x+y-10i)(3x-6y-36j)(19x+95y-95k)\right|,$$ where $x,y$ are real numbers.
Four spheres have radii $2,2,3,3$, respectively, and each is externally tangent to the other three. A further sphere is externally tangent to all four. Determine its radius.
Let $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{10}$ be pairwise distinct natural numbers whose sum is $1995$. Find the minimum value of $$a_1a_2+a_2a_3+\cdots+a_9a_{10}+a_{10}a_1.$$

Let $n>1$ be odd. Define $x_k=(x_1^{(k)},\ldots,x_n^{(k)})$ by $x_0=(1,0,\ldots,0,1)$ and, for $k\ge1$, $$x_i^{(k)}=\begin{cases}0,&x_i^{(k-1)}=x_{i+1}^{(k-1)},\\1,&x_i^{(k-1)}\ne x_{i+1}^{(k-1)},\end{cases}\qquad 1\le i\le n,$$ with cyclic subscripts, so $x_{n+1}^{(k-1)}=x_1^{(k-1)}$. If $m$ is a positive integer and $x_m=x_0$, prove that $n\mid m$.
Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with orthocentre $H$. The tangents from $A$ to the circle with diameter $BC$ touch it at $P,Q$. Prove that $H,P,Q$ are collinear.
Find the smallest positive integer $K$ such that every $K$-element subset of $\{1,2,\ldots,50\}$ contains distinct $a,b$ for which $a+b$ divides $ab$.
Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $$f(x^3+y^3)=(x+y)\bigl(f(x)^2-f(x)f(y)+f(y)^2\bigr)$$ for all real $x,y$. Prove that $f(1996x)=1996f(x)$ for every real $x$.

Eight singers take part in a festival. An organizer schedules $m$ concerts, with four singers performing at each concert. Every pair of singers must perform together the same number of times. Find a schedule minimizing $m$.

Let $n$ be a natural number, $x_0=0$ and $x_i>0$ for $1\le i\le n$, with $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i=1$. Prove that $$1\le\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{x_i}{\sqrt{1+x_0+x_1+\cdots+x_{i-1}}\sqrt{x_i+x_{i+1}+\cdots+x_n}}<\frac\pi2.$$

In triangle $ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\angle A=30^\circ$ and $BC=1$. Find the minimum possible length of the longest side of an inscribed triangle, whose three vertices lie on the three sides of $ABC$, respectively.

Real numbers $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_{1997}$ satisfy $$-\frac1{\sqrt3}\le x_i\le\sqrt3\quad(1\le i\le1997),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^{1997}x_i=-318\sqrt3.$$ Find the maximum value of $$\sum_{i=1}^{1997}x_i^{12}$$ and justify your answer.

Let $A_1B_1C_1D_1$ be a convex quadrilateral and let $P$ lie in its interior. At each vertex, the segment joining that vertex to $P$ makes an acute angle with each of the two incident sides. For $k\ge2$, define $A_k,B_k,C_k,D_k$ as the reflections of $P$ in the lines $A_{k-1}B_{k-1},B_{k-1}C_{k-1},C_{k-1}D_{k-1},D_{k-1}A_{k-1}$, respectively. (a) Which of the first twelve quadrilaterals are necessarily similar to the 1997th, and which are not necessarily similar? (b) If the 1997th quadrilateral is cyclic, which of the first twelve must be cyclic, and which need not be? Prove each necessary conclusion and give counterexamples for the others.

Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ for which the integers $1,2,\ldots,3n$ can be arranged, each used once, in a three-row array $$\begin{matrix}a_1&a_2&\cdots&a_n\\b_1&b_2&\cdots&b_n\\c_1&c_2&\cdots&c_n\end{matrix}$$ such that all column sums are equal and divisible by $6$, and all row sums are equal and divisible by $6$.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral. The extensions of $AB$ and $DC$ meet at $P$, and the extensions of $AD$ and $BC$ meet at $Q$. The two tangents from $Q$ to the circumcircle touch it at $E$ and $F$. Prove that $P,E,F$ are collinear.

Let $A=\{1,2,\ldots,17\}$ and let $f:A\to A$ be a bijection. Define $f^{[1]}=f$ and $f^{[k+1]}=f\circ f^{[k]}$ for positive integers $k$. Suppose there is a positive integer $M$ such that, for every $1\le m<M$ and $1\le i\le16$, $$f^{[m]}(i+1)-f^{[m]}(i)\not\equiv\pm1\pmod{17},\qquad f^{[m]}(1)-f^{[m]}(17)\not\equiv\pm1\pmod{17},$$ whereas $$f^{[M]}(i+1)-f^{[M]}(i)\equiv\pm1\pmod{17}\quad(1\le i\le16),\qquad f^{[M]}(1)-f^{[M]}(17)\equiv\pm1\pmod{17}.$$ Find the largest possible $M$ over all such bijections, and prove your answer.

Let $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers satisfying $$a_{n+m}\le a_n+a_m$$ for all positive integers $m,n$. Prove that, whenever $n\ge m\ge1$, $$a_n\le ma_1+\left(\frac nm-1\right)a_m.$$
Let $ABC$ be a non-obtuse triangle with $AB>AC$ and $\angle B=45^\circ$. Its circumcentre $O$ and incentre $I$ satisfy $\sqrt2\,OI=AB-AC$. Find $\sin A$.

For a given positive integer $n>1$, determine, with proof, whether there exist $2n$ pairwise distinct positive integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n,b_1,\ldots,b_n$ such that $$\sum_{i=1}^n a_i=\sum_{i=1}^n b_i,\qquad n-1>\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{a_i-b_i}{a_i+b_i}>n-1-\frac1{1998}.$$

Let $S=\{1,2,\ldots,98\}$. Find the least natural number $n$ such that every $n$-element subset of $S$ contains ten numbers with this property: however these ten numbers are divided into two groups of five, one group contains a number coprime to each of the other four numbers in that group, and the other group contains a number not coprime to any of the other four numbers in that group.
Find all natural numbers $n>3$ such that $$1+\binom n1+\binom n2+\binom n3\mid 2^{2000}.$$
Let $D$ be a point inside an acute triangle $ABC$ such that $$DA\cdot DB\cdot AB+DB\cdot DC\cdot BC+DC\cdot DA\cdot CA=AB\cdot BC\cdot CA.$$ Determine, with proof, the geometric position of $D$.
Let $n\ge2$ and let $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ be real numbers satisfying $$\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2+\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}x_ix_{i+1}=1.$$ For each $k$ with $1\le k\le n$, find the maximum value of $|x_k|$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $\angle C>\angle B$. Let $D$ lie on $BC$ with $\angle ADB$ obtuse, and let $H$ be the orthocentre of $ABD$. Let $F$ lie inside $ABC$ and on the circumcircle of $ABD$. Prove that $F$ is the orthocentre of $ABC$ if and only if $HD\parallel CF$ and $H$ lies on the circumcircle of $ABC$.

Let $a$ be real. Define polynomials $f_n(x)$ by $f_0(x)=1$ and $$f_{n+1}(x)=xf_n(x)+f_n(ax)\qquad(n\ge0).$$ (a) Prove that $f_n(x)=x^nf_n(x^{-1})$ for every nonnegative integer $n$. (b) Find an explicit expression for $f_n(x)$.

There are $99$ space stations, with a tunnel joining each pair. Exactly $99$ tunnels allow travel in both directions; every other tunnel allows travel in only one direction. A set of four stations is called connected if one can travel from each station to every other station in the set using only the six tunnels joining these four stations. Determine the maximum possible number of connected sets of four stations.
Let $m$ be a positive integer. Prove that there are integers $a,b,k$, with $a,b$ odd and $k\ge0$, such that $$2m=a^{19}+b^{99}+k\,2^{1999}.$$

Find the largest real constant $\lambda$ such that, for every cubic polynomial $f(x)=x^3+ax^2+bx+c$ whose roots are all nonnegative, $$f(x)\ge\lambda(x-a)^3\qquad\text{for all }x\ge0.$$ Determine the equality condition.

A $4\times4\times4$ cube consists of $64$ unit cubes. Select $16$ unit cubes and color them red. A coloring is interesting if every $1\times1\times4$ rectangular box consisting of four unit cubes contains exactly one red unit cube. Determine the number of interesting colorings.
The side lengths $a,b,c$ of triangle $ABC$ satisfy $a\le b\le c$. Its circumradius and inradius are $R,r$, respectively. Let $f=a+b-2R-2r$. Determine the sign of $f$ in terms of $\angle C$.

Define a sequence by $a_1=0$, $a_2=1$, and $$a_n=\frac n2a_{n-1}+\frac{n(n-1)}2a_{n-2}+(-1)^n\left(1-\frac n2\right)\qquad(n\ge3).$$ Find a closed-form expression for $$f_n=a_n+2\binom n1a_{n-1}+3\binom n2a_{n-2}+\cdots+(n-1)\binom n{n-2}a_2+n\binom n{n-1}a_1.$$

A table tennis club schedules doubles matches subject to these rules: (i) each player belongs to at most two pairs; (ii) two distinct pairs play against one another at most once; (iii) players belonging to the same pair never play against one another while partnered with others. The set of distinct numbers of matches played by the individual players is called the set of games. Given a set $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}$ of positive integers, each divisible by $6$, determine the minimum number of players needed for a schedule whose set of games is exactly $A$.

For an ordered real $n$-tuple $A=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$, where $n\ge2$, define $b_k=\max\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}$ and $B=(b_1,\ldots,b_n)$. Call $B$ the innovated tuple of $A$, and call the number of distinct entries of $B$ the innovated degree of $A$. Among all permutations of $1,2,\ldots,n$ whose innovated degree is $2$, find the arithmetic mean of their first entries.
Find all positive integers $n$ for which there exist a positive integer $k$ and integers $n_1,\ldots,n_k>3$ satisfying $$n=n_1n_2\cdots n_k=2^{\frac{(n_1-1)(n_2-1)\cdots(n_k-1)}{2^k}}-1.$$

A test has five multiple-choice questions, each with four options. Each examinee selects one option for each question. Among $2000$ answer sheets there is a number $n$ such that every set of $n$ sheets contains four sheets any two of which agree on at most three answers. Find the minimum possible value of $n$.

Let $\sqrt2<a<2$. Let $ABCD$ be a convex cyclic quadrilateral with its circumcentre in its interior. Its circumcircle $\omega$ has radius $1$, and its longest and shortest sides have lengths $a$ and $\sqrt{4-a^2}$, respectively. The tangents to $\omega$ at $A,B,C,D$ are $L_A,L_B,L_C,L_D$. Put $A\prime=L_A\cap L_B$, $B\prime=L_B\cap L_C$, $C\prime=L_C\cap L_D$, $D\prime=L_D\cap L_A$. Determine the maximum and minimum possible values of $$\frac{S_{A\prime B\prime C\prime D\prime}}{S_{ABCD}}.$$

Let $X=\{1,2,\ldots,2001\}$. Find the least positive integer $m$ such that every $m$-element subset $W$ of $X$ contains $u,v$, not necessarily distinct, for which $u+v=2^k$ for some positive integer $k$.

Let $A_1A_2\cdots A_n$ be a regular $n$-gon. Find all positive integers $n$ such that, for every permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, there are indices $i,j,k$ for which the triangles $A_iA_jA_k$ and $A_{\sigma(i)}A_{\sigma(j)}A_{\sigma(k)}$ are both acute, both right, or both obtuse.

Let $a,b,c$ be positive integers such that $a,b,c,a+b-c,a+c-b,b+c-a,a+b+c$ are seven distinct primes. Two of $a,b,c$ have sum $800$. Find the maximum possible difference between the largest and smallest of the seven primes.

A regular $24$-gon $P_1P_2\cdots P_{24}$ is inscribed in a circle of circumference $24$. Determine the number of sets of eight vertices such that no arc between two chosen vertices has length $3$ or $8$.

Let $a=2001$, and let $A$ consist of all pairs of positive integers $(m,n)$ satisfying $$m<2a,\qquad 2n\mid(2am-m^2+n^2),\qquad n^2-m^2+2mn\le2a(n-m).$$ For $(m,n)\in A$, define $$f(m,n)=\frac{2am-m^2-mn}{n}.$$ Determine the maximum and minimum values of $f$.

Triangle $ABC$ has side lengths $a=BC$, $b=CA$, $c=AB$, with $b<c$. Its internal angle bisector $AD$ meets $BC$ at $D$. (1) Find a necessary and sufficient condition, expressed in terms of $\angle A,\angle B,\angle C$, for the existence of points $E,F$ in the interiors of $AB,AC$, respectively, such that $BE=CF$ and $\angle BDE=\angle CDF$. (2) When such points exist, express $BE$ in terms of $a,b,c$.

Let polynomials $p_n(x)$ satisfy $$p_1(x)=x^2-1,\qquad p_2(x)=2x(x^2-1),$$ and $$p_{n+1}(x)p_{n-1}(x)=p_n(x)^2-(x^2-1)^2\qquad(n\ge2).$$ Let $s_n$ be the sum of the absolute values of the coefficients of $p_n(x)$. For each $n$, find a nonnegative integer $k_n$ such that $2^{-k_n}s_n$ is odd.

Eighteen teams play a round-robin tournament over $17$ rounds. In each round the teams are divided into nine pairs, with one match in each pair, so that every pair of teams meets exactly once during the tournament. Find the largest $n$ such that, after any $n$ rounds of any valid schedule, there always exist four teams between which exactly one match has been played.
For four distinct points $P_1,P_2,P_3,P_4$ in the plane, find the minimum possible value of $$\frac{\sum_{1\le i<j\le4}P_iP_j}{\min_{1\le i<j\le4}P_iP_j}.$$

A point of the plane is called good if both its coordinates are rational. Prove that the good points can be partitioned into three sets such that: (1) the interior of every circle whose centre is good contains a point from each set; (2) no three collinear points belong to three different sets.

Let $\frac12<c<1$. Find the least constant $M$ such that, for every integer $n\ge2$ and every sequence of real numbers $0<a_1\le\cdots\le a_n$ satisfying $$\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n ka_k=c\sum_{k=1}^n a_k,$$ one has $$\sum_{k=1}^n a_k\le M\sum_{k=1}^m a_k,\qquad m=\lfloor cn\rfloor.$$

Let $I$ and $H$ be the incentre and orthocentre of an acute triangle $ABC$, and let $B_1$ and $C_1$ be the midpoints of $AC$ and $AB$, respectively. Ray $B_1I$ intersects $AB$ at $B_2\ne B$, and ray $C_1I$ intersects the extension of $AC$ at $C_2\ne C$. Lines $B_2C_2$ and $BC$ meet at $K$. Let $A_1$ be the circumcentre of triangle $BHC$. Prove that $A,I,A_1$ are collinear if and only if triangles $BKB_2$ and $CKC_2$ have equal areas.

Find the maximum cardinality of a set $S$ of positive integers not exceeding $100$ with the following properties. For any two distinct elements $a,b\in S$, there is $c\in S$ such that $\gcd(a,c)=\gcd(b,c)=1$, and there is $d\in S\setminus\{a,b\}$ such that $\gcd(a,d)>1$ and $\gcd(b,d)>1$.

Given a positive integer $n$, find the least positive real number $\lambda$ such that $$\sum_{i=1}^{n}\cos\theta_i\le\lambda$$ whenever $\theta_i\in(0,\pi/2)$ for $1\le i\le n$ and $$\prod_{i=1}^{n}\tan\theta_i=2^{n/2}.$$
Find all triples of positive integers $(a,m,n)$ with $a\ge2$ and $m\ge2$ such that $$a^m+1\mid a^n+203.$$

Ten applicants with distinct abilities, ranked from best ($1$) to worst ($10$), are interviewed in a uniformly random order. The first three applicants are rejected. From the fourth onwards, the first applicant better than every previously interviewed applicant is hired and interviewing stops. If none of the first nine is hired, the tenth is hired. Let $P_k$ be the probability that the applicant ranked $k$ is hired. Prove that (a) $P_1>P_2>\cdots>P_8=P_9=P_{10}$; (b) $P_1+P_2+P_3>0.7$; (c) $P_8+P_9+P_{10}\le0.1$.

Let $a,b,c,d$ be positive real numbers satisfying $ab+cd=1$, and let $x_i,y_i$ be real numbers with $x_i^2+y_i^2=1$ for $i=1,2,3,4$. Prove that $$(ay_1+by_2+cy_3+dy_4)^2+(ax_4+bx_3+cx_2+dx_1)^2\le2\left(\frac{a^2+b^2}{ab}+\frac{c^2+d^2}{cd}\right).$$

Let $EFGH$, $ABCD$ and $E_1F_1G_1H_1$ be convex quadrilaterals. Points $E,F,G,H$ lie on $AB,BC,CD,DA$, respectively, and $$\frac{AE}{EB}\frac{BF}{FC}\frac{CG}{GD}\frac{DH}{HA}=1.$$ Points $A,B,C,D$ lie on $H_1E_1,E_1F_1,F_1G_1,G_1H_1$, respectively, and $E_1F_1\parallel EF$, $F_1G_1\parallel FG$, $G_1H_1\parallel GH$, $H_1E_1\parallel HE$. If $E_1A/AH_1=\lambda$, express $F_1C/CG_1$ in terms of $\lambda$.
Let $c$ be a positive integer. Define $x_1=c$ and, for $n\ge2$, $$x_n=x_{n-1}+\left\lfloor\frac{2x_{n-1}-(n+2)}{n}\right\rfloor+1.$$ Find an expression for $x_n$ in terms of $n$ and $c$.

A set $M$ of $n$ points in the plane contains the vertices of a convex heptagon. Whenever five points of $M$ are the vertices of a convex pentagon, another point of $M$ lies in its interior. Find the minimum possible value of $n$.

For a real number $a$ and a positive integer $n$, prove that there is exactly one sequence of real numbers $x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_n,x_{n+1}$ satisfying $$x_0=x_{n+1}=0,\qquad\frac12(x_{i+1}+x_{i-1})=x_i+x_i^3-a^3\quad(1\le i\le n).$$ Prove also that $|x_i|\le|a|$ for $0\le i\le n+1$.

Let $n\ge2$ and let $a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_n$ be positive integers satisfying $\sum_{i=1}^{n}1/a_i\le1$. Prove that, for every real $x$, $$\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac1{a_i^2+x^2}\right)^2\le\frac1{2\bigl(a_1(a_1-1)+x^2\bigr)}.$$

Prove that every positive integer $n$, with finitely many exceptions, can be written as $$n=a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_{2004},$$ where $1\le a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_{2004}$ are integers and $a_i\mid a_{i+1}$ for $1\le i\le2003$.

Suppose $\theta_i \in \left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ for $i = 1, 2, 3, 4$. Prove that there exists $x \in \mathbb{R}$ satisfying both inequalities $$\cos^2\theta_1\cos^2\theta_2 - (\sin\theta_1\sin\theta_2 - x)^2 \ge 0, \qquad \cos^2\theta_3\cos^2\theta_4 - (\sin\theta_3\sin\theta_4 - x)^2 \ge 0$$ if and only if $$\sum_{i=1}^{4}\sin^2\theta_i \le 2\left(1 + \prod_{i=1}^{4}\sin\theta_i + \prod_{i=1}^{4}\cos\theta_i\right).$$

A circle meets the three sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$ of a triangle $ABC$ at points $D_1, D_2$; $E_1, E_2$; $F_1, F_2$, respectively, in the order $D_1,D_2$ along $BC$, $E_1,E_2$ along $CA$, and $F_1,F_2$ along $AB$. Line segments $D_1E_1$ and $D_2F_2$ intersect at $L$, line segments $E_1F_1$ and $E_2D_2$ intersect at $M$, and line segments $F_1D_1$ and $F_2E_2$ intersect at $N$. Prove that the lines $AL$, $BM$, $CN$ are concurrent.

As shown in the figure, a pond is divided into $2n$ parts ($n \ge 5$). Two parts are called neighbors if they have a common side or arc, so every part has exactly three neighbors. There are $4n + 1$ frogs in the pond. Whenever a part contains three or more frogs, three of the frogs in that part jump to its three neighbors, one to each. Prove that after some time the frogs will be distributed uniformly, that is, for every part, either there are frogs in that part or there are frogs in each of its neighbors.

The sequence $\{a_n\}$ is defined by $a_1 = \dfrac{21}{16}$ and, for $n \ge 2$, $$2a_n - 3a_{n-1} = \frac{3}{2^{n+1}}.$$ Let $m \ge 2$ be an integer. Prove that for $n \le m$, $$\left(a_n + \frac{3}{2^{n+3}}\right)^{\frac{1}{m}}\left(m - \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{\frac{n(m-1)}{m}}\right) < \frac{m^2 - 1}{m - n + 1}.$$

There are $5$ points in a rectangle of area $1$ (boundary included), no three of which are collinear. Find the minimum number of triangles with vertices among these five points whose area is not greater than $\frac{1}{4}$.
Find all nonnegative integer solutions $(x, y, z, w)$ of the equation $$2^x \cdot 3^y - 5^z \cdot 7^w = 1.$$
Let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be real numbers satisfying $a_1+\cdots+a_n=0$. Prove that $$\max_{1\le i\le n}a_i^2\le\frac n3\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(a_i-a_{i+1})^2.$$

Positive integers $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{2006}$ satisfy the condition that the $2005$ ratios $a_1/a_2,a_2/a_3,\ldots,a_{2005}/a_{2006}$ are pairwise distinct. Find the minimum possible number of distinct values among $a_1,\ldots,a_{2006}$.
Positive integers $m,n,k$ satisfy $mn=k^2+k+3$. Prove that at least one of the equations $$x^2+11y^2=4m,\qquad x^2+11y^2=4n$$ has an integer solution $(x,y)$ with both $x$ and $y$ odd.

Let $ABC$ be a right triangle with $\angle ACB=90^\circ$. Its incircle touches $BC,CA,AB$ at $D,E,F$, respectively. Line $AD$ intersects the incircle again at $P$. If $\angle BPC=90^\circ$, prove that $AE+AP=PD$.

Define $a_1=\frac12$ and $$a_{k+1}=-a_k+\frac1{2-a_k}\qquad(k\ge1).$$ Prove that, for every positive integer $n$, $$\left(\frac{n}{2(a_1+\cdots+a_n)}-1\right)^n\le\left(\frac{a_1+\cdots+a_n}{n}\right)^n\prod_{i=1}^{n}\left(\frac1{a_i}-1\right).$$

Let $X$ be a set of $56$ elements. Find the least positive integer $n$ with the following property: for any $15$ subsets of $X$, if the union of every seven of these subsets contains at least $n$ elements, then three of the $15$ subsets have nonempty intersection.
Let $a,b,c$ be complex numbers, and put $m=|a+b|$, $n=|a-b|$. If $mn\ne0$, prove that $$\max\{|ac+b|,|a+bc|\}\ge\frac{mn}{\sqrt{m^2+n^2}}.$$

Prove both statements: (1) If $2n-1$ is prime, then for every choice of $n$ pairwise distinct positive integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, there are $i,j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that $$\frac{a_i+a_j}{\gcd(a_i,a_j)}\ge2n-1.$$ (2) If $2n-1$ is composite, there exist $n$ pairwise distinct positive integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ such that $$\frac{a_i+a_j}{\gcd(a_i,a_j)}<2n-1$$ for all $i,j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$.

Let $a_1,\ldots,a_{11}$ be pairwise distinct positive integers with sum less than $2007$. Begin with the ordered sequence $S=(1,2,\ldots,2007)$. An operation consists of $22$ successive steps: at step $i$, choose an entry $x$ of the current sequence and replace it with $x+a_i$ if $1\le i\le11$, or with $x-a_{i-11}$ if $12\le i\le22$. Call the operation odd or even if its final sequence is, respectively, an odd or even permutation of $1,\ldots,2007$. Which is larger, the number of odd operations or the number of even operations, and by how much? A permutation $(x_1,\ldots,x_{2007})$ is even when $\prod_{i>j}(x_i-x_j)>0$, and odd otherwise.

Let $O,I$ be the circumcentre and incentre of triangle $ABC$. Its incircle touches $BC,CA,AB$ at $D,E,F$, respectively. Lines $FD,ED$ meet $CA,AB$ at $P,Q$, respectively. Let $M,N$ be the midpoints of $PE,QF$. Prove that $OI\perp MN$.
Let $(a_n)_{n\ge1}$ be a bounded sequence satisfying $$a_n<\sum_{k=n}^{2n+2006}\frac{a_k}{k+1}+\frac1{2n+2007}\qquad(n=1,2,3,\ldots).$$ Prove that $a_n<1/n$ for every positive integer $n$.

Find the smallest integer $n\ge9$ such that, for any $n$ integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, not necessarily distinct, there are indices $1\le i_1<\cdots<i_9\le n$ and coefficients $b_1,\ldots,b_9\in\{4,7\}$ for which $$b_1a_{i_1}+b_2a_{i_2}+\cdots+b_9a_{i_9}$$ is divisible by $9$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute scalene triangle with circumcentre $O$. Let $A\prime$ lie on the extension of segment $AO$ such that $\angle BA\prime A=\angle CA\prime A$. Let $A_1,A_2$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $A\prime$ to $AC,AB$, respectively, and let $H_A$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$. Let $R_A$ be the circumradius of $H_AA_1A_2$, and define $R_B,R_C$ cyclically. Prove that $$\frac1{R_A}+\frac1{R_B}+\frac1{R_C}=\frac2R,$$ where $R$ is the circumradius of $ABC$.

For an integer $n\ge3$, prove that $X=\{1,2,\ldots,n^2-n\}$ can be partitioned into two nonempty sets such that neither contains $n$ elements $a_1<\cdots<a_n$ satisfying $$a_k\le\frac{a_{k-1}+a_{k+1}}2\qquad(2\le k\le n-1).$$

Let $n$ be a positive integer and let real numbers $x_1\le\cdots\le x_n$ and $y_1\ge\cdots\ge y_n$ satisfy $$\sum_{i=1}^n ix_i=\sum_{i=1}^n iy_i.$$ Prove that, for every real $\alpha$, $$\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\lfloor i\alpha\rfloor\ge\sum_{i=1}^n y_i\lfloor i\alpha\rfloor.$$ Here $\lfloor\beta\rfloor$ is the greatest integer not exceeding $\beta$.

Let $A$ be an infinite subset of the positive integers, and let $n>1$ be a fixed integer. Suppose that, for every prime $p$ not dividing $n$, infinitely many elements of $A$ are not divisible by $p$. Prove that, for every integer $m>1$ with $\gcd(m,n)=1$, there is a finite set of distinct elements of $A$ whose sum is congruent to $1$ modulo $m$ and to $0$ modulo $n$.

Find the smallest integer $n$ such that every coloring of the vertices of a regular $n$-gon with red, yellow or blue contains four vertices of the same color forming an isosceles trapezoid. Here an isosceles trapezoid has one pair of parallel sides and a pair of equal nonparallel sides; rectangles are excluded.
Find all triples $(p,q,n)$ satisfying $$q^{n+2}\equiv3^{n+2}\pmod{p^n},\qquad p^{n+2}\equiv3^{n+2}\pmod{q^n},$$ where $p,q$ are odd primes and $n$ is an integer greater than $1$.

In an acute triangle $PBC$ with $PB\ne PC$, points $A,D$ lie on sides $PB,PC$, respectively. Let $M,N$ be the midpoints of $BC,AD$, and let $O=AC\cap BD$. The perpendiculars from $O$ to lines $AB,CD$ meet them at $E,F$, respectively. (a) Prove that if $A,B,C,D$ are concyclic, then $EM\cdot FN=EN\cdot FM$. (b) Does this equality imply that $A,B,C,D$ are concyclic? Justify your answer.
Find all pairs of prime numbers $(p,q)$ for which $pq\mid 5^p+5^q$.
Let $m,n$ be integers with $4<m<n$. A regular $(2n+1)$-gon has vertices $A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_{2n+1}$. How many convex $m$-gons whose vertices belong to this set have exactly two acute interior angles?
Let $n\ge3$ be an integer. Real numbers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ satisfy $\min_{1\le i<j\le n}|a_i-a_j|=1$. Find the minimum of $\sum_{k=1}^{n}|a_k|^3$.

The sides and diagonals of a convex $n$-gon are coloured with $n$ given colours, one colour per segment. For every choice of three distinct colours, there is a triangle with vertices among the polygon vertices whose three sides have those colours. Determine all possible values of $n$.

For every integer $n\ge3$, prove that there is a set $S$ of $n$ distinct positive integers such that, for any two distinct nonempty subsets $A,B\subseteq S$, the numbers $\frac{1}{|A|}\sum_{x\in A}x$ and $\frac{1}{|B|}\sum_{x\in B}x$ are coprime composite integers.

Two circles $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$ intersect at $A,B$. A line through $B$ meets them again at $C,D$, respectively; another line through $B$ meets them again at $E,F$, respectively. Line $CF$ meets $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$ again at $P,Q$, respectively. Let $M,N$ be the midpoints of arcs $PB,QB$, respectively, as in the figure. If $CD=EF$, prove that $C,F,M,N$ are concyclic.

Let $k\ge3$ be an integer. A sequence is defined by $a_k=2k$ and, for $n>k$, $a_n=a_{n-1}+1$ if $\gcd(a_{n-1},n)=1$, and $a_n=2n$ otherwise. Prove that $a_n-a_{n-1}$ is prime for infinitely many $n>k$.
Complex numbers $a,b,c$ satisfy $|az^2+bz+c|\le1$ for every complex number $z$ with $|z|\le1$. Find the maximum possible value of $|bc|$.

Let $m,n>1$ be integers and let $a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_m$ be integers. Prove that there is a set $T$ of integers with $|T|\le1+\frac{a_m-a_1}{2n+1}$ such that each $a_i$ can be expressed as $a_i=t+s$, where $t\in T$ and $s$ is an integer in $[-n,n]$.

Let $n\ge3$. Cards are distributed among $n+1$ piles $A_1,\ldots,A_n,O$, with cyclic indices $A_0=A_n$ and $A_{n+1}=A_1$. Two moves are allowed: (1) if $A_i$ has at least three cards, remove three from it and add one to each of $A_{i-1},A_{i+1},O$; (2) if $O$ has at least $n$ cards, remove $n$ from it and add one to each $A_i$. Prove that if the total number of cards is at least $n^2+3n+1$, a finite sequence of moves can leave at least $n+1$ cards in every pile.

Let $a_1,a_2,a_3,b_1,b_2,b_3$ be six pairwise distinct positive integers. For every positive integer $n$, assume that $(n+1)a_1^n+n a_2^n+(n-1)a_3^n$ divides $(n+1)b_1^n+n b_2^n+(n-1)b_3^n$. Prove that there is a positive integer $k$ such that $b_i=k a_i$ for $i=1,2,3$.

Let $n\ge3$ and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be real numbers. Put $a_{n+1}=a_1$, $M=\max_{1\le i\le n}a_i$ and $m=\min_{1\le i\le n}a_i$. Prove that $\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i^2-\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i a_{i+1}\le\left\lfloor\frac n2\right\rfloor(M-m)^2$.

In the configuration shown, $D$ is the midpoint of arc $BC$ of the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Point $X$ lies on arc $BD$, $E$ is the midpoint of arc $AX$, and $S$ lies on arc $AC$. Lines $SD,BC$ meet at $R$, and lines $SE,AX$ meet at $T$. If $RT\parallel DE$, prove that the incentre of triangle $ABC$ lies on line $RT$.

Let $A$ be a finite set of real numbers, and let $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ be nonempty subsets of $A$. Suppose that the sum of all elements of $A$ is zero, and that every choice $x_i\in A_i$ for $i=1,\ldots,n$ satisfies $x_1+\cdots+x_n>0$. Prove that for some $1\le k\le n$ and $1\le i_1<\cdots<i_k\le n$, $|A_{i_1}\cup\cdots\cup A_{i_k}|<\frac{k}{n}|A|$. Here $|X|$ denotes the cardinality of a finite set $X$.

For a given positive integer $n$, put $S=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. Find the minimum of $|A\triangle S|+|B\triangle S|+|C\triangle S|$ over nonempty finite sets $A,B$ of real numbers, where $C=\{a+b:a\in A,\ b\in B\}$. The symbol $\triangle$ denotes symmetric difference and $|X|$ denotes cardinality.

Let $n\ge4$ be an integer. Nonnegative real numbers $a_1,\ldots,a_n,b_1,\ldots,b_n$ satisfy $a_1+\cdots+a_n=b_1+\cdots+b_n>0$. Find the maximum of $\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i(a_i+b_i)}{\sum_{i=1}^{n}b_i(a_i+b_i)}$.
For any given positive integers $m,n$, prove that there are infinitely many pairs of coprime positive integers $a,b$ such that $a+b\mid a m^a+b n^b$.

In triangle $ABC$, angle $A$ is the largest. On its circumcircle, let $D$ and $E$ be the midpoints of arcs $ABC$ and $ACB$, respectively. Circle $O_1$ passes through $A,B$ and is tangent to line $AC$ at $A$; circle $O_2$ passes through $A,E$ and is tangent to line $AD$ at $A$. The circles intersect again at $P$. Prove that $AP$ bisects $\angle BAC$.

Let $p$ be a prime. Arrange the integers $1,2,\ldots,p^2$, each used exactly once, in a $p\times p$ matrix. A move adds $1$ to every entry in one row or one column, or subtracts $1$ from every entry in one row or one column. An arrangement is good if finitely many moves can make every entry zero. How many good arrangements are there?

For every real number $M>2$, prove that there is an infinite strictly increasing sequence of positive integers $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ such that (1) $a_i>M^i$ for every positive integer $i$; (2) an integer $n$ is nonzero if and only if there are a positive integer $m$ and signs $b_1,\ldots,b_m\in\{-1,1\}$ with $n=\sum_{i=1}^{m}b_i a_i$.

Let $a,b$ be positive real numbers, let $n\ge2$ be an integer, and put $f(x)=(x+a)(x+b)$. For nonnegative real numbers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ with $x_1+\cdots+x_n=1$, find the maximum of $\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}\min\{f(x_i),f(x_j)\}$.

Let $n$ be a square-free positive even integer, $k$ an integer, and $p$ a prime satisfying $p<2\sqrt n$, $p\nmid n$ and $p\mid n+k^2$. Prove that $n=ab+bc+ca$ for some pairwise distinct positive integers $a,b,c$.
Find the smallest positive integer $k$ such that every $k$-element subset $A$ of $S=\{1,2,\ldots,2012\}$ contains all three numbers $a+b,b+c,c+a$ for some pairwise distinct elements $a,b,c\in S$.

Two circles $K_1,K_2$ of different radii intersect at $A,B$. Points $C\in K_1$ and $D\in K_2$ satisfy that $A$ is the midpoint of $CD$. The extension of $DB$ meets $K_1$ again at $E$, and the extension of $CB$ meets $K_2$ again at $F$. Let $\ell_1,\ell_2$ be the perpendicular bisectors of $CD,EF$, respectively. (1) Prove that $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ have a unique common point $P$. (2) Prove that $CA,AP,PE$ are the side lengths of a right triangle.

Find all nonempty sets $S$ of integers such that $3m-2n\in S$ for all $m,n\in S$, including $m=n$.

Find all positive real numbers $t$ for which there is an infinite set $X$ of real numbers such that $\max\{|x-(a-d)|,|y-a|,|z-(a+d)|\}>td$ for all $x,y,z\in X$ (not necessarily distinct), all real $a$, and all positive real $d$.

Let $n\ge2$ be an integer. Nonempty finite sets $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ satisfy $|A_i\triangle A_j|=|i-j|$ for all $i,j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Find the minimum of $\sum_{i=1}^{n}|A_i|$. Here $\triangle$ denotes symmetric difference and $|X|$ denotes cardinality.

For each positive integer $n$ and $0\le i\le n$, let $c(n,i)\in\{0,1\}$ be defined by $c(n,i)\equiv\binom ni\pmod2$, and put $f(n,q)=\sum_{i=0}^{n}c(n,i)q^i$. Let $m,n,q$ be positive integers such that $q+1$ is not a power of $2$. If $f(m,q)\mid f(n,q)$, prove that $f(m,r)\mid f(n,r)$ for every positive integer $r$.

Given positive integers $m,n$, find the smallest integer $N\ge m$ such that every $N$-element set of integers containing a complete residue system modulo $m$ has a nonempty subset whose element sum is divisible by $n$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB>AC$. Its internal angle bisector from $A$ meets $BC$ at $D$. Points $E,F$ lie on sides $AB,AC$, respectively, and $B,C,F,E$ are concyclic. Prove that the circumcentre of triangle $DEF$ is the incentre of triangle $ABC$ if and only if $BE+CF=BC$.

For an integer $n>1$, define $D(n)=\{a-b:a,b\text{ are positive integers},\ ab=n,\ a>b\}$. Prove that for every integer $k>1$, there are pairwise distinct integers $n_1,\ldots,n_k>1$ such that $D(n_1)\cap\cdots\cap D(n_k)$ contains at least two elements.

Prove that there is a unique function $f:\mathbb N^*\to\mathbb N^*$ satisfying $f(1)=f(2)=1$ and $f(n)=f(f(n-1))+f(n-f(n-1))$ for every integer $n\ge3$, where $\mathbb N^*$ is the set of positive integers. For each integer $m\ge2$, determine $f(2^m)$.

For an integer $n>1$ with prime factorisation $n=p_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots p_t^{\alpha_t}$, write $\omega(n)=t$ and $\Omega(n)=\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_t$. Prove or disprove: for every positive integer $k$ and positive real numbers $\alpha,\beta$, there is an integer $n>1$ such that $\frac{\omega(n+k)}{\omega(n)}>\alpha$ and $\frac{\Omega(n+k)}{\Omega(n)}<\beta$.

Let $X=\{1,2,\ldots,100\}$. Consider functions $f:X\to X$ satisfying (1) $f(x)\ne x$ for every $x\in X$; (2) $A\cap f(A)\ne\varnothing$ for every $A\subseteq X$ with $|A|=40$. Find the smallest positive integer $k$ such that every such function admits a subset $B\subseteq X$ with $|B|=k$ and $B\cup f(B)=X$. Here $f(T)=\{f(t):t\in T\}$.

For nonempty sets $S,T$ of numbers, define $S+T=\{s+t:s\in S,t\in T\}$ and $2S=\{2s:s\in S\}$. Let $n$ be a positive integer and $A,B$ nonempty subsets of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. Prove that there is a subset $D\subseteq A+B$ such that $D+D\subseteq2(A+B)$ and $|D|\ge\frac{|A|\,|B|}{2n}$. Here $|X|$ denotes cardinality.
Let $z_1,z_2,\ldots,z_n$ be complex numbers satisfying $|z_i-1|\le r$ for some $r\in(0,1)$. Prove that $$\left|\sum_{i=1}^n z_i\right|\left|\sum_{i=1}^n\frac1{z_i}\right|\ge n^2(1-r^2).$$

Let $A,B,D,E,F,C$ be six points on a circle, in that order, with $AB=AC$. Define $P=AD\cap BE$, $R=AF\cap CE$, $Q=BF\cap CD$, $S=AD\cap BF$, and $T=AF\cap CD$. Let $K$ lie on $ST$ and satisfy $\angle QKS=\angle ECA$. Prove that $$\frac{SK}{KT}=\frac{PQ}{QR}.$$

Let $n\ge5$ be a positive integer. Let $A\subseteq B$ be sets of integers with $|A|=n$ and $|B|=m$. Suppose that for any distinct $x,y\in B$, $$x+y\in B\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x,y\in A.$$ Determine the minimum possible value of $m$.
Determine all integers $k$ for which there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that $$n+k\nmid\binom{2n}{n}.$$

Among $30$ students, each student has at most $5$ friends, and every set of $5$ students contains a pair who are not friends. Determine the largest integer $k$ such that every configuration satisfying these conditions contains $k$ students no two of whom are friends.

Let $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ be a sequence of nonnegative integers such that, for all positive integers $m,n$, $$\sum_{i=1}^{2m}a_{in}\le m.$$ Prove that there are positive integers $k,d$ such that $$\sum_{i=1}^{2k}a_{id}=k-2014.$$

Let $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{31}$ and $b_1,b_2,\ldots,b_{31}$ be positive integers satisfying $$a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_{31}\le2015,\qquad b_1<b_2<\cdots<b_{31}\le2015,$$ and $$\sum_{i=1}^{31}a_i=\sum_{i=1}^{31}b_i.$$ Find the maximum possible value of $$S=\sum_{i=1}^{31}|a_i-b_i|.$$

In triangle $AEF$, points $B,D$ lie on segments $AE,AF$, respectively, and $ED$ and $FB$ meet at $C$. Points $K,L,M,N$ lie on segments $AB,BC,CD,DA$, respectively, and satisfy $$\frac{AK}{KB}=\frac{AD}{BC},\quad\frac{BL}{LC}=\frac{BA}{CD},\quad\frac{CM}{MD}=\frac{CB}{DA},\quad\frac{DN}{NA}=\frac{DC}{AB}.$$ The incircle of triangle $AEF$ touches $AE,AF$ at $S,T$, respectively; the incircle of triangle $CEF$ touches $CE,CF$ at $U,V$, respectively. Prove that if $K,L,M,N$ are concyclic, then $S,T,U,V$ are concyclic.

Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_p$ be integers. Prove that the following conditions are equivalent: (1) There is a polynomial $P(x)$ of degree at most $(p-1)/2$ such that $P(i)\equiv a_i\pmod p$ for $1\le i\le p$. (2) For every natural number $d\le(p-1)/2$, $$\sum_{i=1}^{p}(a_{i+d}-a_i)^2\equiv0\pmod p,$$ where subscripts are interpreted modulo $p$.

Let $n\ge2$ be a positive integer, and let $k$ be the number of primes at most $n$. Put $S=\{2,3,\ldots,n\}$. Suppose that $A\subseteq S$, $|A|\le k$, and no two distinct elements of $A$ divide one another. Prove that there is a set $B$ with $|B|=k$ and $A\subseteq B\subseteq S$ such that no two distinct elements of $B$ divide one another.

Let $G$ be a complete directed graph on $100$ vertices such that for any two vertices $x,y$ there is a directed path from $x$ to $y$. (a) Prove that there is an integer $m$ such that for any two vertices $x,y$ there is a directed path of length $m$ from $x$ to $y$; vertices may be repeated along a path. (b) For each such graph $G$, let $m(G)$ be the smallest possible $m$ in part (a). Find the minimum value of $m(G)$ over all such graphs.

Let $a,b,c$ be real numbers. Define $u_0=u_1=1$, $u_n=2u_{n-1}-3u_{n-2}$ for $n\ge2$, and $v_0=a$, $v_1=b$, $v_2=c$, $v_n=v_{n-1}-3v_{n-2}+27v_{n-3}$ for $n\ge3$. Suppose that for some positive integer $N$, every $v_n$ with $n\ge N$ is an integer divisible by $u_n$. Prove that $3a=2b+c$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB>AC$, circumcenter $O$ and incenter $I$. Its incircle touches $BC$ at $D$. The tangents to its circumcircle at $B$ and $C$ meet at $L$. Let $X=AO\cap BC$ and let $Y$ be the foot of the altitude from $A$ to $BC$. Let $P,Q$ be the endpoints of the diameter of the circumcircle passing through $I$. Prove that $A,D,L$ are collinear if and only if $P,X,Y,Q$ are concyclic.

A rectangle $R$ is partitioned into $2016$ smaller rectangles whose sides are parallel to the sides of $R$. Call every corner of a smaller rectangle a vertex. A segment lying along the sides of the partition is basic if its endpoints are vertices and its interior contains no other vertex. Find the maximum and minimum possible numbers of basic segments over all such partitions.

Let $n\ge2$ be an integer. Two permutations of $1,2,\ldots,n$ are related by a prefix reversal if one is obtained from the other by reversing its first $k$ entries for some $1\le k\le n$. Prove that all $n!$ permutations can be listed as $P_1,\ldots,P_{n!}$ so that each consecutive pair is related by a prefix reversal, including $P_{n!}$ and $P_1$.

Let $D_n$ be the set of positive divisors of a positive integer $n$. Find all $n$ for which $D_n$ can be partitioned into two disjoint sets $A,G$, each containing at least three elements, such that the elements of $A$ can be arranged in an arithmetic progression and those of $G$ in a geometric progression.
Given an integer $n\ge2$ and real numbers $0<a<b$, find the maximum of $$\frac{x_1^2/x_2+x_2^2/x_3+\cdots+x_{n-1}^2/x_n+x_n^2/x_1}{x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_n}$$ over all $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in[a,b]$.

For a positive integer $n$, let $A_n$ be the set of primes $p$ for which there exist positive integers $a,b$ such that both $(a+b)/p$ and $(a^n+b^n)/p^2$ are integers coprime to $p$. When $A_n$ is finite, including when it is empty, write $f(n)=|A_n|$. (a) Prove that $A_n$ is finite if and only if $n\ne2$. (b) If $k,m$ are odd positive integers and $d=\gcd(k,m)$, prove that $$f(d)\le f(k)+f(m)-f(km)\le2f(d).$$

Let $n,k$ be positive integers and $$T=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb Z^3:1\le x,y,z\le n\}.$$ Suppose that $3n^2-3n+1+k$ points of $T$ are colored red. Whenever two red points determine a segment parallel to a coordinate axis, all lattice points on that segment are red. Prove that at least $k$ distinct unit cubes have all eight vertices red.

Let $q$ be a positive integer that is not a perfect cube. Prove that there exists a real constant $c>0$ such that $$\{nq^{1/3}\}+\{nq^{2/3}\}\ge c n^{-1/2}$$ for every positive integer $n$, where $\{x\}$ denotes the fractional part of $x$.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral whose diagonals meet at $P$. The circumcircle of $APD$ meets segment $AB$ again at $E$, and the circumcircle of $BPC$ meets segment $AB$ again at $F$. Let $I,J$ be the incenters of triangles $ADE,BCF$, respectively, and let $K=IJ\cap AC$. Prove that $A,I,K,E$ are concyclic.

Let $n\ge3$ be odd. Color every square of an $n\times n$ board black or white. Two squares are adjacent if they have the same color and share a vertex. Squares are connected if they can be joined by a chain of adjacent squares. Find the largest integer $M$ for which some coloring admits $M$ pairwise unconnected squares.

Let $n>k$ be positive integers and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in(k-1,k)$. Positive real numbers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ satisfy $$\sum_{i\in I}x_i\le\sum_{i\in I}a_i$$ for every $k$-element subset $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Find the maximum possible value of $x_1x_2\cdots x_n$.
Real numbers $a,b,c,d,e\ge-1$ satisfy $a+b+c+d+e=5$. Find the minimum and maximum values of $$(a+b)(b+c)(c+d)(d+e)(e+a).$$

A Pythagorean set is a set of three positive integers that are the side lengths of a right triangle. Prove that for any two Pythagorean sets $P,Q$, there are $m\ge2$ Pythagorean sets $P_1,\ldots,P_m$ with $P_1=P$, $P_m=Q$ and $P_i\cap P_{i+1}\ne\varnothing$ for every $1\le i<m$.

Triangle $ABC$, with $AB<AC$, has circumcenter $O$. Point $D$ lies on the internal angle-bisector line of $\angle BAC$. Point $E$ lies on $BC$ with $OE\parallel AD$ and $DE\perp BC$. Point $K$ lies on ray $EB$ beyond $B$ and satisfies $EK=EA$. The circle through $A,D,K$ meets line $BC$ again at $P$ and the circumcircle of $ABC$ again at $Q$. Prove that $PQ$ is tangent to the circumcircle of $ABC$.

An ellipse that is not a circle is given. (a) Prove that there is a unique rhombus of minimum area whose four sides are tangent to the ellipse. (b) Give a straightedge-and-compass construction of this rhombus.

An integer is written in each cell of an $n\times n$ board. A move chooses one cell and adds $1$ to all $2n-1$ entries in its row or column. Find the largest integer $N(n)$ such that, for every initial board, finitely many moves can produce at least $N(n)$ even entries.

Place $2018$ points $P_1,\ldots,P_{2018}$ inside or on the boundary of a fixed regular pentagon; points may coincide. Find all arrangements maximizing $$\sum_{1\le i<j\le2018}|P_iP_j|^2,$$ and prove your answer.

Let $a_1,\ldots,a_{40}$ be real numbers with $\sum_{i=1}^{40}a_i=0$ and $|a_i-a_{i+1}|\le1$ for $1\le i\le40$, where $a_{41}=a_1$. Find the maximum possible values of (a) $a_{10}+a_{20}+a_{30}+a_{40}$ and (b) $a_{10}a_{20}+a_{30}a_{40}$.

In triangle $ABC$ with $AB>AC$, the bisector of $\angle BAC$ meets $BC$ at $D$. Point $P$ lies on ray $DA$ beyond $A$. From $P$, draw tangents $PQ$ and $PR$ to the circumcircles of $ABD$ and $ACD$, respectively, choosing $Q$ on the same side of $AD$ as $B$ and $R$ on the same side as $C$. Let $K=BR\cap CQ$. The line through $K$ parallel to $BC$ meets $QD,AD,RD$ at $E,L,F$, respectively. Prove that $EL=FK$.

Let $S$ be a set with $35$ elements and $\mathcal F$ a family of maps $S\to S$. Say that $\mathcal F$ has property $P(k)$ if for every $x,y\in S$ there exist $f_1,\ldots,f_k\in\mathcal F$, not necessarily distinct, such that $$f_k(\cdots f_2(f_1(x))\cdots)=f_k(\cdots f_2(f_1(y))\cdots).$$ Find the least positive integer $m$ such that every family with $P(2019)$ also has $P(m)$.

Find the largest real constant $c$ with the following property for every integer $n\ge3$: if $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ are closed arcs of a circle and at least half of the $\binom n3$ triples have nonempty common intersection, then some set $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ satisfies $|I|>cn$ and $\bigcap_{i\in I}A_i\ne\varnothing$.

For an integer $t>1$, let $P(t)$ be its largest prime factor. A sequence of positive integers is defined by $a_1>1$ and $a_{n+1}=a_n+P(a_n)$ for $n\ge1$. Prove that the sequence contains a perfect square.

Do there exist positive real numbers $a_0,\ldots,a_{19}$ such that $$P(x)=x^{20}+a_{19}x^{19}+\cdots+a_1x+a_0$$ has no real root, but interchanging any two coefficients $a_i,a_j$ with $0\le i<j\le19$ produces a polynomial with a real root? Prove your answer.

Let $(z_n)_{n\ge1}$ be a complex sequence with real odd-indexed terms and purely imaginary even-indexed terms, satisfying $|z_kz_{k+1}|=2^k$ for every positive integer $k$. Put $f_n=|z_1+\cdots+z_n|$. Find the minimum possible values of (a) $f_{2020}$ and (b) $f_{2020}f_{2021}$.

Let $m>1$ be an integer. Find the smallest positive integer $n$ such that for any integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n,b_1,\ldots,b_n$ there exist integers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ with at least one $x_i$ coprime to $m$ and $$\sum_{i=1}^n a_ix_i\equiv\sum_{i=1}^n b_ix_i\equiv0\pmod m.$$

Let $n$ be a positive integer divisible by exactly $36$ distinct primes. For $k=1,\ldots,5$, let $c_k$ count the integers coprime to $n$ in the closed interval $[(k-1)n/5,kn/5]$. Suppose that $c_1,\ldots,c_5$ are not all equal. Prove that $$\sum_{1\le i<j\le5}(c_i-c_j)^2\ge2^{36}.$$

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB>AC$, circumcenter $O$ and circumcircle $\omega$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of the minor arc $BC$, and let $K$ be the point of $\omega$ diametrically opposite $A$. The line through $O$ parallel to $AM$ meets segment $AB$ at $D$ and ray $CA$ beyond $A$ at $E$. Put $P=BM\cap CK$, $Q=CM\cap BK$. Prove that $$\angle OEB+\angle OPB=\angle ODC+\angle OQC.$$

A convex polyhedron has exactly three faces meeting at each vertex and an even number of $k$-gonal faces for every $k\ge3$. An ant starts at the midpoint of an edge, travels along a simple closed route consisting of edges, and returns to its starting point without visiting any other point twice. The route divides the surface into two regions containing equal numbers of $k$-gonal faces for every $k$. Prove that the ant makes equally many left turns and right turns at vertices.
Find all functions $f:\mathbb Z_{>0}\to\mathbb Z_{>0}$ such that $$f(f(x)+y)\mid x+f(y)$$ for all positive integers $x,y$.

Fix positive real numbers $a,b$ and a segment $AB$ of length $a$ in the plane. Variable points $C,D$ form a nondegenerate convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ with $BC=CD=b$ and $DA=a$. Its four sides are tangent to a circle with center $I$. Determine the exact locus of $I$.

Find the largest real number $\lambda$ such that for every choice of positive real numbers $p,q,r,s$ there is a complex number $z=a+bi$, with $a,b\in\mathbb R$, satisfying $$|b|\ge\lambda|a|,\qquad (pz^3+2qz^2+2rz+s)(qz^3+2pz^2+2sz+r)=0.$$
Find all positive integers $a$ for which there exists a set $X$ of six integers such that for every $k=1,2,\ldots,36$ there are $x,y\in X$ with $$ax+y\equiv k\pmod{37}.$$

A conference has $n\ge3$ scientists, each with at least one friend among the others. Friendship is mutual. Every partition into two nonempty groups has a pair of friends in the same group and a pair of friends in different groups. On the first day, each scientist expresses an opinion as a nonnegative integer. On each subsequent day, every scientist replaces their opinion by the floor of the average of their friends' opinions on the preceding day. Prove that eventually all scientists have the same opinion.

A sheet of paper is marked with two points at distance $1$ and nothing else. Prove that a straightedge and compass can construct a line and two points on it at distance $\sqrt{2021}$, using at most ten distinct lines and circles in total. Give explicit construction steps and number the lines and circles in the order they are drawn.

For integers $0\le a\le n$, let $f(n,a)$ be the number of coefficients divisible by $3$ in the expansion of $(x+1)^a(x+2)^{n-a}$. For instance, $f(4,3)=1$. For each positive integer $n$, put $$F(n)=\min_{0\le a\le n}f(n,a).$$ Prove that (a) $F(n)\ge(n-1)/3$ for infinitely many positive integers $n$, and (b) $F(n)\le(n-1)/3$ for every positive integer $n$.

Positive real sequences $(a_n),(b_n)$ satisfy $$a_{n+1}=a_n-\frac1{1+\sum_{i=1}^n1/a_i},\qquad b_{n+1}=b_n+\frac1{1+\sum_{i=1}^n1/b_i}.$$ (a) If $a_{100}b_{100}=a_{101}b_{101}$, find $a_1-b_1$. (b) If $a_{100}=b_{99}$, compare $a_{100}+b_{100}$ with $a_{101}+b_{101}$.

Let $ABC$ be an equilateral triangle of side length $1$. Points $D,E,F$ lie in the interiors of $BC,CA,AB$, respectively, with $DE/20=EF/22=FD/38$. Points $X,Y,Z$ lie on lines $BC,CA,AB$, respectively, with $XY\perp DE$, $YZ\perp EF$, $ZX\perp FD$. Find all possible values of $$\frac1{[DEF]}+\frac1{[XYZ]},$$ where brackets denote triangle area.

Color the vertices of a regular $(2m+2n)$-gon, where $m,n$ are positive integers, with $2m$ black and $2n$ white vertices. The coloring distance between two vertices of the same color is the smaller number of opposite-colored vertices on the two boundary paths joining them. A black matching pairs all black vertices with $m$ pairwise nonintersecting segments; define $P(B)$ as the sum of the coloring distances of its pairs. Define a white matching and $P(W)$ analogously using all $2n$ white vertices. Prove that $$\max_B P(B)=\max_W P(W)$$ for every coloring.

Find the smallest integer $n\ge3$ for which there are planar points $A_1,\ldots,A_n$, no three collinear, such that for every $i$ some segment $A_jA_{j+1}$ with $j\ne i$ passes through the midpoint of $A_iA_{i+1}$. Indices are cyclic, so $A_{n+1}=A_1$.

Prove that there is a constant $C>0$ such that every infinite arithmetic progression of positive integers $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ with squarefree $\gcd(a_1,a_2)$ has a squarefree term $a_m$ with $m\le C a_2^2$. An integer is squarefree if it is not divisible by the square of any integer greater than $1$.

There are $n\ge8$ airports with directed nonstop routes. For any two distinct airports, there is at most one route in each direction. For every nonempty proper set $A$ of airports, at least $4\min\{|A|,n-|A|\}$ routes go from $A$ to its complement. Prove that from every airport $x$ one can travel along at most $\sqrt{2n}$ routes and return to $x$.
Find the smallest real $\lambda$ such that every positive integer $n$ can be written as $n=x_1x_2\cdots x_{2023}$ with positive integers $x_i$, each of which is either prime or at most $n^\lambda$.
Find the largest real constant $c$ such that $$\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n(n-|i-j|)x_ix_j\ge c\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2$$ for every positive integer $n$ and all real numbers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$.

Let $p\ge5$ be prime and $S=\{1,\ldots,p\}$. For $x,y\in S$, define $r(x,y)=y-x$ if $y\ge x$ and $r(x,y)=y-x+p$ otherwise. For a nonempty proper subset $A\subset S$, put $$f(A)=\sum_{x\in A}\sum_{y\in A}r(x,y)^2.$$ Call $A$ good if $f(B)\ge f(A)$ for every $B\subseteq S$ with $|B|=|A|$. Find the largest integer $L$ for which there are distinct good sets $A_1\subset A_2\subset\cdots\subset A_L$.
Nonnegative real numbers $a_1,\ldots,a_{2023}$ have sum $100$. Let $$A=\{(i,j):1\le i\le j\le2023,\ a_ia_j\ge1\}.$$ Find the maximum possible value of $|A|$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle and let $K$ lie on ray $BC$ beyond $C$. Draw rays $KP,KQ$ parallel to and in the same directions as rays $AB,AC$, respectively, choosing $P,Q$ distinct from $K$ with $BP=BK$ and $CQ=CK$. The circumcircle of $KPQ$ meets line $AK$ again at $T$. Prove that (a) $\angle BTC+\angle APB=\angle CQA$ and (b) $AP\cdot BT\cdot CQ=AQ\cdot CT\cdot BP$.

Label the vertices of a regular $99$-gon with the integers $1,\ldots,99$, each used once. Labelings agreeing under a rotation are identified. A move swaps the labels at two adjacent vertices. Find the smallest integer $n$ such that any labeling can be transformed into any other with at most $n$ moves.

Let $\alpha>1$ be irrational and let $L$ be a positive integer with $L>\alpha^2/(\alpha-1)$. Starting from a positive integer $x_1>L$, define $$x_{n+1}=\begin{cases}\lfloor\alpha x_n\rfloor,&x_n\le L,\\\lfloor x_n/\alpha\rfloor,&x_n>L.\end{cases}$$ Prove that the sequence is eventually periodic and that its eventual least positive period is odd and independent of $x_1$.

Triangle $ABC$ has incenter $I$. Let $L,M,N$ be the midpoints of $AI,AC,CI$, respectively. Point $D$ lies on segment $AM$ with $BD=BC$. The incircle of $ABD$ touches $AD,BD$ at $E,F$, respectively. Let $J$ be the circumcenter of $AIC$, and let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of $JMD$. Lines $MN$ and $JL$ meet $\omega$ again at $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Prove that $PQ,LN,EF$ are concurrent.

Let $a_1>a_2>\cdots>a_n>1$ be integers and put $M=\operatorname{lcm}(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$. For a finite nonempty set $X$ of positive integers, define $$f(X)=\min_{1\le i\le n}\sum_{x\in X}\left\{\frac{x}{a_i}\right\},$$ where braces denote fractional part, and set $f(\varnothing)=0$. Call $X$ minimal if $f(Y)<f(X)$ for every proper subset $Y\subset X$. If $X$ is minimal and $f(X)\ge2/a_n$, prove that $|X|\le f(X)M$.

Define the fractional distance between planar points $(x_1,y_1)$ and $(x_2,y_2)$ by $$\sqrt{\|x_1-x_2\|^2+\|y_1-y_2\|^2},$$ where $\|t\|$ is the distance from $t$ to the nearest integer. Find the largest real $r$ for which four planar points can have all six pairwise fractional distances at least $r$.

For a prime $p$, consider bijections $f:\{0,1,\ldots,p-1\}\to\{0,1,\ldots,p-1\}$ satisfying $|f(a)-f(b)|\le2024$ whenever $p\mid a^2-b$. Prove that infinitely many primes admit such a bijection and infinitely many primes do not.

Real numbers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ satisfy $$\sum_{i=1}^n a_i=n,\qquad\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2=2n,\qquad\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^3=3n.$$ (a) Find the largest constant $C$ such that $$\max_i a_i-\min_i a_i\ge C$$ for all $n\ge4$. (b) Prove that there is a constant $C_2>0$, independent of $n$ and the numbers, such that $$\max_i a_i-\min_i a_i\ge C+C_2 n^{-3/2}.$$
Define $$A=\{re^{i\theta}:r\ge0,\ 0\le\theta\le\pi/41\},\qquad B=\{x+iy:x,y\in\mathbb R,\ |x-y|<2025\}.$$ Find all polynomials $P$ with complex coefficients such that $P(z)\in B$ for every $z\in A$.

A convex cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ has circumcenter $O$, circumradius $1$ and $\angle ABC<\angle BCD<90^\circ$. Let $P=BA\cap CD$ and $Q=AC\cap BD$. Suppose that some point $K$ on segment $BC$ satisfies that $P,A,K,D$ are concyclic and $KB\cdot KC=OP^2/2$. The perpendicular to $BC$ through $Q$ meets line $OP$ at $T$. Find all possible values of (a) $OP$ and (b) $TB+TC$.

Initially, $n$ red cards each carry $0$, and $n$ blue cards each carry $1$. A move chooses a red card with a smaller number than a blue card and replaces both numbers by their arithmetic mean. Find the smallest positive integer $n$ for which finitely many moves can make the sum of the numbers on the red cards greater than $100$.

There are thirty colors of cards, seventy cards of each color. Choose any seventy cards and arrange them in a stack. A move selects a card $X$ among the bottom twenty whose color is absent from the top fifty, selects a card $Y$ among the top fifty whose color occurs there at least twice, and moves $X$ immediately above $Y$. Repeat until no eligible $X$ remains. Prove that every sequence of moves terminates, and find the maximum possible number of moves over all initial stacks and choices.

Find all real numbers $\lambda$ for which there exists $N>0$ such that, for every integer $n\ge N$ and all nonnegative real numbers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ with sum $1$, $$\left(\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}x_ix_j\right)^2\le\lambda\sum_{1\le i<j<k\le n}x_ix_jx_k+\frac1n\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}(x_i-x_j)^2.$$

Let $n\ge3$ be odd and satisfy $\gcd(p-1,n)=1$ for every prime divisor $p$ of $n$. Count the triples $(a,b,c)\in\{1,2,\ldots,n\}^3$ such that $\gcd(a,b,c,n)=1$ and there exists a permutation $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ of $1,\ldots,n$ with $$ax_{k+2}+bx_{k+1}+cx_k\equiv0\pmod n$$ for every $1\le k\le n$, where indices are cyclic.
